newsitem.title: UK: London coffee futures opens down $120 at $1,700.
newsitem.headline: London coffee futures opens down $120 at $1,700.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures opened sharply lower on Wednesday, with July down $120 at $1,700 per tonne and then quickly extending its losses.

July's drop to the lowest since May 2 came after a weak close in New York on Tuesday, when panicky speculators dumped their holdings on forecasts of milder weather in key producer Brazil. July closed down 35.35 cents at 217.95 cents per pound on Tuesday after hitting a one-month low.
Brazil had seen some chilly nights recently, which had raised fears of a damaging frost like that of 1994, when prices last soared, traders said.
But such worries were eased when weather forecasters said temperatures in the country's key coffee regions should edge up in coming days and no damaging cold was foreseeable in the near term.

September robusta coffee broke initial support at $1,772, a 61.8 percent retracement of its bull run dating back to January. It also broke next support at $1,710. But a wide band of support rests between $1,700 and $1,550, a range established from activity between February and May, technical analysts said.
